title: German Cities — Opportunity-Card (Chancenkarte) Relocation Scoreboard
subtitle: Scored for a Bangladeshi software engineer on a 1-year job-seeking visa: register → rent → job → EU Blue Card conversion

detail.summary: The best all-rounder for this plan — no weak link in the land-and-convert core.
detail.note: Blue Card runs through the Hamburg Welcome Center, a dedicated English-friendly skilled-worker channel (~8–12 weeks), not a general Ausländerbehörde queue.

pros.text: Welcome Center conversion is faster + more English-friendly than Berlin/Munich's general offices.
Sponsor-heavy market (Airbus, Otto/About You, Google, gaming, growing AI/climatetech); rents well below Munich/Frankfurt.
Diverse, western, low far-right risk; real Bangladeshi anchor (Steindamm South-Asian strip).

cons.text: Deep-tech/AI-research depth trails Berlin/Munich.
Entry-level saturated (300–400 applications/role); Anmeldung slots go fast.

methodology: Overall is the weighted mean of the 11 scored criteria (weights shown), computed live over the criteria present — raw, no display curve. Scores are evidence-backed 0–100 expert synthesis: no single index ranks e.g. 'Blue Card conversion speed by city', so each cell is built from official processing-time statements, rent indices (GREIX Q4 2025 + city Mietspiegel), job-posting counts, election results and hate-crime statistics. The land-and-convert cluster — Conversion (16) + Jobs (14) + Anmeldung (10) + English (9) = 49 — plus Competition (8) reflects the stated priority: land a full-time tech job and convert the EU Blue Card inside the 12-month Chancenkarte window. Context columns (population, rent, salary, community, embassy) are descriptive, not scored. Chancenkarte basics: up to 12 months, part-time work ≤20 h/week + 2-week trials, proof of funds €1,091/month (€13,092/year, 2026); Blue Card IT/shortage salary bar €43,759.80 (2025); settlement in 21 months with B1 German (27 with A1).
caveats: The spread is narrow (60.5–70.1) — a tie-break among viable cities, not a quality gap. Your specialisation, savings and how fast you land an offer move the needle more than the city choice.
Bureaucracy speed is the highest-variance input; only Leipzig and Berlin publish clear signals. Verify your target office's current Ausländerbehörde/Bürgeramt waits before committing.
Rents are new-lease/asking figures (GREIX Q4 2025 for the big cities; ImmoScout24/Numbeo/Mietspiegel elsewhere), re-accelerating at end-2025 (~+4.5% YoY) — budget upward.
Safety is national/regional, not street-level: anti-Islamic hate crimes rose ~140% in 2023; the east/west split (Saxony's Dresden/Leipzig higher-risk) is the main per-city differentiator.

Salary bands are cross-checked market aggregates (Glassdoor/Levels.fyi/StepStone), not official; most mid-level offers clear the 2025 Blue Card IT bar (€43,759.80). Bangladeshi community sizes are dual-sourced only where a city register publishes them (Munich, Nuremberg); elsewhere they are qualitative.
